weeks.title: What a Business Is: Purpose, Stakeholders and Forms
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki business kya hota hai, uska purpose kya hai, kaun-kaun stakeholders hote hain, aur India mein business ke common forms (proprietorship, partnership, LLP, company, cooperative) kaise alag hain.
concepts: **Business** ek economic activity hai jisme goods ya services ka production ya exchange regular basis par, profit ke liye aur risk lekar kiya jaata hai. Ek baar ki sale ya hobby business nahi hai; regularity, profit motive aur uncertainty teeno chahiye.

**Purpose of business**: Profit zaroori hai (survival, growth aur risk ka reward), par Peter Drucker ka point tha ki business ka asli purpose customer create karna aur retain karna hai. Profit is baat ka test hai ki business kitna achha kaam kar raha hai, khud purpose nahi. Objectives economic, social, human aur national, chaaron tarah ke hote hain.

**Stakeholders** woh sab hain jin par business ka asar padta hai ya jo business par asar daalte hain. Internal: owners/shareholders, managers, employees. External: customers, suppliers, lenders, government, local community aur environment. Inke interests aksar takraate hain, jaise shareholders zyada dividend chahte hain aur employees zyada salary.

**Shareholder view vs stakeholder view**: Milton Friedman jaise thinkers ke hisaab se business ki main zimmedari kaanoon ke andar rehkar owners ka profit badhana hai. R. Edward Freeman ka stakeholder view kehta hai ki manager ko sabhi stakeholders ke interests balance karne chahiye. Real decisions mein dono soch dikhti hain.

**Sole proprietorship**: Ek hi owner, formation aasaan, saara profit owner ka, par **unlimited liability** (business ke karz ke liye owner ki personal property bhi ja sakti hai), limited capital aur continuity ka risk. Mohalle ki kirana dukaan typical example hai.

**Partnership aur LLP**: General partnership (Indian Partnership Act, 1932) mein partners ki liability unlimited aur joint hoti hai, aur har partner doosron ko bind kar sakta hai (mutual agency). **LLP** (LLP Act, 2008) ek separate legal entity hai jisme partners ki liability limited hoti hai, par partnership jaisi flexibility bhi milti hai.

**Company** (Companies Act, 2013): separate legal entity, shareholders ki **limited liability**, **perpetual succession** (members aate-jaate rahein, company chalti rehti hai) aur ownership-management ka separation. Private company: kam se kam 2 aur zyada se zyada 200 members, shares transfer par restriction. Public company: kam se kam 7 members, shares freely transferable, stock exchange par list ho sakti hai. One Person Company (OPC) mein ek hi member hota hai.

**Cooperative aur public sector**: Cooperative society mein 'one member, one vote' hota hai aur service motive pehle aata hai (Amul jaise dairy cooperatives). Public sector enterprises mein government ownership hoti hai. Form chunne ke factors: kitna capital chahiye, liability kitni lena chahte ho, control, continuity aur compliance ka cost.

example.problem: Neha 'Masala Mornings' (fictional) naam ki breakfast chain shuru karna chahti hai. Use 4 doston se paisa chahiye, woh nahi chahti ki business ke karz ke liye uska ghar risk mein ho, aur woh shares aur board meetings ka heavy compliance abhi avoid karna chahti hai. Kaunsa form sabse suitable hai?
steps: Sole proprietorship hata do: ek hi owner hota hai aur liability unlimited hai, dono requirements fail.
General partnership: 5 log aa sakte hain, par liability unlimited aur joint hai, isliye ghar risk mein rahega.
Private company: limited liability milti hai, par shares, board aur zyada compliance chahiye, jo Neha abhi nahi chahti.
LLP: separate legal entity, partners ki liability limited, aur partnership jaisa flexible internal agreement.
Answer: **LLP** sabse achha fit hai. Baad mein bade investors laane hon to private company mein convert karne ka socha ja sakta hai.

mistakes: Business ka matlab sirf profit samajhna. Profit zaroori hai, par customer, employees aur society ko ignore karne wala business lambe samay tak survive nahi karta. Exam mein 'purpose' aur 'objective' wale options dhyaan se padho.
Limited aur unlimited liability ulta yaad rakhna. Proprietorship aur general partnership = unlimited; company aur LLP = limited. Trick: jahan 'separate legal entity' hai, wahan liability limited hai.

Perpetual succession ka matlab 'company kabhi band nahi hogi' samajhna. Iska matlab hai ki members ki death ya exit se company ka existence khatam nahi hota; legal process (winding up) se company band ho sakti hai.
revision: Business = regular activity + profit motive + risk.
Drucker: purpose customer create karna; profit performance ka test.
Stakeholders: shareholders, employees, customers, suppliers, lenders, government, community.
Unlimited liability: proprietorship, general partnership. Limited: LLP, company.
Private company 2 se 200 members; public company kam se kam 7.
Company aur LLP separate legal entities hain; perpetual succession company ki khaasiyat hai.

questions.question: Riya ne apni purani almirah ek baar online beech di aur use thoda profit bhi hua. Kya ye business activity hai?
options: Nahi, kyunki ye ek baar ki sale hai, regular activity nahi
Haan, kyunki buyer aur seller dono maujood hain
questions.explanation: Business ke liye activity ka regular hona zaroori hai, saath mein profit motive aur risk. Ek baar purana saamaan bechna personal sale hai. Trap: sirf profit dekh kar 'haan' bol dena; profit akela kaafi nahi.

questions.question: Ek sole proprietor ka business doob gaya. Lenders ne apna paisa wapas lene ke liye owner ka personal flat bhi bikwa diya. Ye kis feature ki wajah se hua?
questions.explanation: Sole proprietorship mein owner aur business legally alag nahi hote, isliye owner ki liability unlimited hoti hai aur personal assets se bhi karz chukaya ja sakta hai. Separate legal entity aur limited liability company/LLP ke features hain, jo ulta owner ko bachaate.

questions.question: 'Neelgiri Textiles' (fictional) ek chhote shehar ka plant band karke cost kam karna chahti hai. Isse share price badhegi, par workers aur local dukaandaar nuksaan uthayenge. Sirf in baaton ke base par kaunsa view is decision ko sabse strongly support karega?
options: Shareholder view: kaanoon ke andar rehkar owners ka return maximise karna main zimmedari hai
Stakeholder view: sabhi affected groups ke interests ko barabar weight dena
Cooperative principle: one member, one vote
questions.explanation: Friedman-style shareholder view kehta hai ki legal limits ke andar owners ka profit badhana business ki main zimmedari hai, isliye share price badhne wala decision ise suit karta hai. Stakeholder view workers aur community ke nuksaan ko bhi weight deta, to woh is decision par sawaal uthata. Unity of command ka is sawaal se koi lena-dena nahi.

questions.question: Kis business form mein ye teeno baatein ek saath milti hain: separate legal entity, partners ki limited liability, aur partners khud business chalaate hain bina shares issue kiye?
questions.explanation: LLP separate legal entity hai, partners ki liability limited hoti hai aur internal management partnership agreement se chalta hai, shares se nahi. General partnership mein liability unlimited hai; public company mein shares aur board hote hain. Sabse tempting trap general partnership hai, kyunki naam mein 'partnership' hai.

questions.question: Ek private company ke founder aur sabse bade shareholder ki achanak death ho jaati hai. Company ka kya hoga?
options: Company apne aap dissolve ho jaayegi
Company chalti rahegi; founder ke shares legal heirs ke paas jaayenge
Company heir ki sole proprietorship ban jaayegi
questions.explanation: Company ka perpetual succession hota hai: woh apne members se alag legal person hai, isliye kisi member ki death se uska existence khatam nahi hota. Shares transmission se heirs ke paas chale jaate hain. Trap: proprietorship ki tarah sochna, jahan owner ke saath business bhi khatam ho sakta hai.

questions.question: Business ke purpose aur profit ke baare mein Peter Drucker ki soch ko kaunsa statement sabse sahi capture karta hai?
options: Purpose customer create aur retain karna hai; profit performance ka test aur future mein bane rehne ka cost hai, khud purpose nahi
Purpose sirf profit maximise karna hai; customers bas uska zariya hain
Purpose social welfare hai, isliye profit se bachna chahiye
Purpose employment dena hai; customers secondary hain
questions.explanation: Drucker ke hisaab se business tabhi exist karta hai jab woh customer ki need poori kare, isliye purpose customer create karna hai. Profit zaroori hai, par woh is baat ka test hai ki business sahi kaam kar raha hai aur future risks ke liye zaroori cost hai. Sabse tempting trap 'profit maximisation' hai, jo Drucker ki soch ka ulta hai, aur 'profit se bachna' bhi galat hai kyunki Drucker profit ko zaroori maante the.

questions.question: 'Chai Junction' (fictional) ek tea stall chain hai. Inme se kaunsa uska external stakeholder hai?
options: Chain ke senior managers aur supervisors
Stalls par kaam karne wale employees
Chain mein paisa lagaane wale owners
Stalls ke aas-paas ki local community
questions.explanation: Internal stakeholders organisation ke andar hote hain: owners, managers aur employees. Local community bahar se affect hoti hai (traffic, kachra, rozgaar), isliye external stakeholder hai. Trap: employees ko external samajhna kyunki woh owner nahi hain; par woh organisation ke andar kaam karte hain, isliye internal hain.

questions.question: Ek dairy cooperative society mein 500 members hain. Ek member ke paas 100 shares hain aur doosre ke paas sirf 2. General meeting mein voting kaise hogi?
options: Har member ka ek hi vote hoga
Har share par ek vote hoga
Sirf sabse bade member ka vote chalega
questions.explanation: Cooperative ka basic principle 'one member, one vote' hai: shares kitne bhi hon, har member ka ek vote. Isse control paise ke bajaye members ke haath mein rehta hai. Trap: 'har share par ek vote', jo company ka rule hai, cooperative ka nahi.

questions.question: Companies Act, 2013 ke hisaab se ek private company mein zyada se zyada kitne members ho sakte hain?
questions.explanation: Private company mein kam se kam 2 aur zyada se zyada 200 members ho sakte hain. 7 public company ka minimum hai, upper limit nahi. 50 purane Companies Act, 1956 ki limit thi. 'Koi limit nahi' public company ke liye sahi hai, private ke liye nahi.

questions.question: 'Lohit Steel' (fictional) apne factory workers ke liye safe working conditions, skill training aur fair wages ko apna ek objective banaati hai. Business objectives ke chaar types mein se ye kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: Jo objectives business ke apne employees ki welfare, satisfaction aur growth se jude hon, woh human objectives hain. Social objectives bahar ke samaaj ke liye hote hain (jaise community, consumers ko fair deal), aur national objectives desh ke goals ke liye (jaise exports, employment). Trap: social objective, kyunki welfare shabd samaaj jaisa lagta hai, par yahan beneficiary company ke andar ke workers hain.

questions.question: 'Rao Traders' (fictional) ek general partnership hai. Ek partner ne business ke normal kaam ke liye firm ke naam par ₹5 lakh ka maal order kiya, baaki partners se pooche bina. Firm payment nahi kar paati. Supplier paisa kahan se le sakta hai?
options: Firm se, aur zaroorat pade to kisi bhi partner ki personal property se
Sirf us partner se jisne bina pooche order diya tha
Kisi se nahi, kyunki baaki partners ne approve nahi kiya
Sirf firm ke assets se, kyunki partners ki liability limited hai
questions.explanation: Mutual agency ki wajah se har partner business ke normal kaam mein firm ko bind karta hai, isliye order poori firm par laagu hai. General partnership mein liability unlimited hai, isliye firm ke assets kam padein to kisi bhi partner ki personal property se recovery ho sakti hai. 'Liability limited hai' LLP ka feature hai, general partnership ka nahi; aur approval na hona supplier ke khilaaf defence nahi hai.

questions.question: Arjun ek software consultancy shuru kar raha hai. Teen conditions hain: (1) agle 3 saal mein venture capital investors aayenge jo equity shares lenge, (2) founders ki liability limited honi chahiye, (3) shares abhi public ko nahi bechne aur stock exchange par list nahi karna. Kaunsa form sabse fit hai?
questions.explanation: Step 1: equity shares chahiye, isliye company form chahiye; LLP aur partnership shares issue nahi karte. Step 2: limited liability chahiye, jo company mein milti hai. Step 3: public ko shares nahi bechne, isliye private company (restricted transfer, listing nahi). Trap: LLP, kyunki usme limited liability hai, par woh equity shares issue nahi kar sakti, jo investors ki main need hai. Public company listing aur zyada compliance laati hai, jo condition 3 ke khilaaf hai.

questions.question: 'Megha Foods' (fictional) ke paas ₹10 crore ka extra profit hai. Teen proposals: (P) poora paisa shareholders ko special dividend, (Q) poora paisa employees ka bonus, (R) aadha dividend aur aadha workers ki training aur paas ke gaon ka water project. Sirf in baaton ke base par, Freeman ka stakeholder view kise sabse zyada support karega aur Friedman ka shareholder view kise?
options: Stakeholder view: P; shareholder view: R
Stakeholder view: Q; shareholder view: Q
Stakeholder view: R; shareholder view: P
Stakeholder view: P; shareholder view: P
questions.explanation: Freeman ka stakeholder view sabhi affected groups ke interests balance karna chahta hai; R shareholders, workers aur community teeno ko kuch deta hai. Friedman ke hisaab se kaanoon ke andar owners ka return badhana main zimmedari hai, isliye P. Trap: Q ko stakeholder view maanna; Q sirf ek group (employees) ko sab de deta hai, jo balance nahi, bas favour shift karna hai.

questions.question: A, B aur C ki general partnership firm par ₹30 lakh ka karz hai aur firm ke assets sirf ₹12 lakh ke hain. A aur B ke paas koi personal property nahi, C ke paas ₹25 lakh ki property hai. Agar ye LLP hoti to creditors ko kul kitna milta, aur general partnership mein C ko apni property se zyada se zyada kitna dena pad sakta hai?
questions.explanation: LLP mein partners ki liability limited hai, isliye creditors ko sirf firm ke assets, yaani ₹12 lakh milte. General partnership mein shortfall = 30 − 12 = ₹18 lakh; liability unlimited aur joint hai, isliye creditors poora ₹18 lakh C se le sakte hain (C baad mein A aur B se unka hissa maang sakta hai). Trap: ₹6 lakh = 18 ÷ 3 baraabar hissa maan lena; ₹25 lakh C ki poori property hai, par karz sirf ₹18 lakh baaki hai.

questions.question: Ek private company ke abhi 170 members hain (sab outside investors). Company 40 naye investors ko shares dena chahti hai. Iske baad company ko kya karna padega?
options: Members 210 ho jaayenge, jo 200 se zyada hai; public company banna padega
Kuch nahi, kyunki private company mein members ki upper limit nahi hoti
LLP mein convert karna padega, kyunki members 7 se zyada hain
Naye investors ki liability unlimited aur baaki ki limited ho jaayegi
questions.explanation: 170 + 40 = 210 members, jabki private company ki maximum limit 200 hai. Isliye itne members ke saath use public company mein convert hona padega (ya naye members kam karne honge). Trap: 7 wala option, kyunki 7 public company ka minimum hai, LLP ka koi rule nahi; aur company mein sab shareholders ki liability limited hi rehti hai, naye ho ya purane.

weeks.title: The Classical School: Taylor, Fayol and Weber
weeks.summary: Is week aap classical school of management seekhoge: Taylor ka scientific management, Fayol ke administrative principles aur Weber ki bureaucracy, aur in teeno ki limitations.
concepts: **Classical school ka background**: Industrial revolution ke baad bade factories aaye, par kaam 'rule of thumb' se hota tha aur wastage bahut tha. Classical thinkers ne management ko systematic banaya. Teen branches: scientific management (shop floor ki efficiency), administrative theory (poori organisation ka management) aur bureaucracy (formal structure).

**Taylor ka scientific management**: F. W. Taylor ne kaha ki har kaam ka ek 'one best way' hota hai jo observation aur measurement se nikalta hai. Tools: **time study** (har step ka time naapna), methods aur tools ka standardisation, workers ka scientific selection aur training, **differential piece-rate** (standard se zyada output par higher rate) aur **functional foremanship** (alag-alag kaam ke liye alag specialist foremen). Unki book 'The Principles of Scientific Management' 1911 mein aayi.

**Mental revolution**: Taylor ke hisaab se management aur workers ko surplus baantne par ladne ke bajaye surplus badhaane par cooperate karna chahiye. Ye scientific management ka attitude wala hissa hai, jo aksar bhool jaate hain.

**Gilbreths aur Gantt**: Frank aur Lillian Gilbreth ne **motion study** ki, yaani kaam ki unnecessary movements hatana (jaise bricklaying ke steps kam karna). Henry Gantt ne **Gantt chart** diya, jisme tasks ko time ke against bars se dikhaya jaata hai, aur task-and-bonus wage system.

**Fayol ki administrative theory**: Henri Fayol ne poori organisation ko upar se dekha. Management ke paanch functions: planning, organising, commanding, coordinating, controlling. Unke **14 principles** flexible guidelines hain, rigid laws nahi.

**Fayol ke important principles**: **Unity of command** (ek employee ka ek hi boss), **unity of direction** (ek objective wali activities ka ek head aur ek plan), division of work, authority aur responsibility saath-saath, **scalar chain** (upar se neeche authority ki line) aur uske andar **gang plank** (same level ke log permission lekar seedhe baat kar sakte hain), order, equity, stability of tenure, initiative aur esprit de corps (team spirit).

**Weber ki bureaucracy**: Max Weber ne ek 'ideal type' organisation describe ki: clear hierarchy, likhe hue rules aur procedures, impersonality (rules sab par barabar), specialisation, technical qualification aur merit par selection-promotion, written records, aur office ownership se alag. Authority ke teen types: traditional, charismatic aur **rational-legal** (bureaucracy ka base).

**Limitations**: Classical school workers ko 'economic man' maanta tha jo sirf paise se motivate hota hai, aur social needs ignore karta tha. Bureaucracy zyada ho to red tape aur rigidity aati hai. Taylor par speed-up aur workers ke exploitation ka criticism hua. Phir bhi aaj ke SOPs, job descriptions aur org charts inhi ideas se aaye hain.

example.problem: 'Pavan Pumps' (fictional) ki assembly line par manager teen workers ko stopwatch se observe karta hai, sabse fast tareeka chunta hai, use SOP bana kar sabko train karta hai, aur standard se zyada output par higher piece rate deta hai. Saath hi woh har worker ko do supervisors ke under rakhta hai: ek quality ke liye, ek speed ke liye. Kaunse ideas use hue aur kahan takraav hai?
steps: Stopwatch se steps naapna aur best method chunna: Taylor ka time study aur 'one best way'.
SOP bana kar sabko train karna: standardisation aur scientific training.
Standard se zyada output par higher rate: differential piece-rate system.
Alag specialist supervisors: Taylor ki functional foremanship.
Par ek worker ke do boss Fayol ke unity of command ko todte hain; conflicting orders aa sakte hain.
Answer: Approach **scientific management** hai, aur functional foremanship ka Fayol ke **unity of command** se takraav hai.

mistakes: Unity of command aur unity of direction mix karna. Command = ek **person** ka ek boss. Direction = ek **objective** ke liye ek plan aur ek head. Sawaal mein 'do boss' dikhe to command, 'do plan' dikhe to direction.
Taylor ko sirf stopwatch tak seemit karna. Mental revolution, scientific selection aur training bhi unke core ideas hain.
Bureaucracy ko sirf 'red tape' samajhna. Weber ke liye bureaucracy fair aur efficient tha kyunki decisions rules aur merit par hote hain, personal pasand par nahi; red tape uska dysfunction hai.
revision: Taylor: one best way, time study, differential piece-rate, functional foremanship, mental revolution.
Gilbreths: motion study. Gantt: Gantt chart.
Fayol: 5 functions + 14 principles; unity of command = one boss.
Gang plank: scalar chain mein same level par seedha contact.
Weber: hierarchy, rules, impersonality, merit, records; rational-legal authority.
Classical school ki kamzori: 'economic man', social needs ignore.

questions.question: Ek warehouse manager stopwatch se packing ke har step ka time naapta hai aur sabse fast standard method sab workers ke liye fix kar deta hai. Ye kis approach ka example hai?
questions.explanation: Time study se 'one best way' nikaal kar standardise karna Taylor ke scientific management ka core hai. Bureaucracy rules aur hierarchy ki baat karti hai, kaam ke steps naapne ki nahi. Human relations social needs par focus karta hai.

questions.question: Ek sales executive ko regional manager kehta hai 'pehle Pune ke clients', aur product manager kehta hai 'pehle naya product demo'. Dono uske boss hain. Fayol ka kaunsa principle toot raha hai?
questions.explanation: Unity of command kehta hai ki ek employee ko sirf ek superior se orders milne chahiye. Yahan do boss conflicting orders de rahe hain. Trap: unity of direction, jo ek objective ke liye ek plan ki baat karta hai, na ki ek person ke kitne boss hain.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa Weber ki ideal bureaucracy ka feature hai?
options: Decisions owner ke prati personal loyalty par hote hain
Leader ka personal charisma authority ka main source hai
Har official apne hisaab se rules badal sakta hai
Selection aur promotion technical qualification par, aur likhe hue rules sab par barabar lagte hain
questions.explanation: Weber ki bureaucracy rational-legal authority par chalti hai: merit-based selection, written rules aur impersonality. Personal loyalty traditional authority hai aur charisma charismatic authority, jinhe Weber ne bureaucracy se alag types maana. Rules badalne ki personal azaadi bureaucracy ke ulta hai.

questions.question: 'Rangoli Paints' (fictional) mein ek hi naye product launch ke liye do alag teams apne-apne plan aur budget ke saath kaam kar rahi hain, aur dono ek hi dealers se alag-alag baat kar rahi hain. Fayol ka kaunsa principle ignore hua hai?
questions.explanation: Unity of direction kehta hai ki same objective wali activities ka ek head aur ek plan hona chahiye. Yahan ek objective (launch) ke do plan chal rahe hain, jisse duplication aur confusion hai. Trap: unity of command; yahan problem kisi ek employee ke do boss hone ki nahi, ek objective ke do plan hone ki hai.

questions.question: Production ka ek supervisor aur marketing ka ek supervisor same level par hain. Urgent order ke liye, apne seniors ko inform karke, woh seedhe aapas mein baat kar lete hain bajaye CEO tak file bhejne ke. Fayol ka ye concept kya kehlaata hai?
options: Scalar chain ke andar gang plank
questions.explanation: Fayol ne scalar chain (authority ki line) ko zaroori maana, par urgent cases mein same level ke employees ko superiors ki jaankari ke saath seedha contact karne diya. Ise gang plank kehte hain. Trap: functional foremanship Taylor ka idea hai (worker ke kai specialist foremen), Fayol ka nahi.

questions.question: Taylor ki functional foremanship mein ek worker ko kai specialist foremen se instructions milti hain. Ye Fayol ke kis principle se takraati hai, aur kyun?
options: Division of work se, kyunki foremen specialised nahi hote
Order se, kyunki tools galat jagah rakhe jaate hain
Unity of command se, kyunki worker ke ek se zyada boss ho jaate hain
Equity se, kyunki foremen ko alag-alag salary milti hai
questions.explanation: Functional foremanship mein worker ko speed boss, inspector, repair boss jaise kai foremen orders dete hain, jabki Fayol ka unity of command ek hi boss maangta hai. Division of work wala option ulta hai: functional foremanship toh specialisation ko hi aage le jaati hai, isliye division of work ke saath fit baithti hai, takraati nahi.

questions.question: Ek kingdom mein raja ka beta hi agla raja banta hai, aur log uski baat isliye maante hain kyunki 'hamesha se aisa hi hota aaya hai'. Weber ke hisaab se ye kaunsi authority hai?
questions.explanation: Jab authority custom aur 'hamesha se aisa hota aaya hai' wali parampara se aati hai, to woh traditional authority hai. Charismatic authority leader ke personal gunon se aati hai, aur rational-legal likhe hue rules aur position se, jo bureaucracy ka base hai. Functional authority Weber ke teen types mein hai hi nahi.

questions.question: Ek project manager har task ko time ke against horizontal bars se dikhata hai, taaki saaf dikhe ki kaunsa kaam kab shuru aur kab khatam hoga. Ye tool kis classical thinker ne diya?
questions.explanation: Tasks ko time ke against bars se dikhaane wala chart Henry Gantt ka Gantt chart hai. Taylor ne time study aur differential piece-rate diya, Gilbreth ne motion study, aur Weber ne bureaucracy. Trap: Taylor, kyunki Gantt unke saathi the, par chart Gantt ka hi contribution hai.

questions.question: Ek packing line par manager dekhta hai ki worker har dabba uthaane ke liye 3 baar jhukta hai. Woh table ki height badal kar ye bekaar movements hata deta hai. Ye kiske idea ka example hai?
questions.explanation: Kaam ki unnecessary body movements dhoondh kar hatana Frank aur Lillian Gilbreth ki motion study hai. Scalar chain authority ki line hai, impersonality rules ko sab par barabar lagana, aur task-and-bonus Gantt ka wage system. Trap: Gantt, kyunki woh bhi efficiency se jude the, par unka focus wages aur scheduling par tha.

questions.question: Taylor ke 'mental revolution' ka sahi matlab kya hai?
options: Workers ko har waqt stopwatch se monitor karte rehna
Har worker ko alag kaam ke specialist foremen dena
Surplus par ladne ke bajaye dono milkar surplus badhaayein
Workers ki psychological testing karke hi unhe hire karna
questions.explanation: Mental revolution attitude ka badlaav hai: management aur workers surplus ke bantwaare par ladne ke bajaye cooperate karke surplus hi bada karein, jisse dono ko zyada mile. Stopwatch monitoring time study ka tool hai aur specialist foremen functional foremanship hai; dono scientific management ke tools hain, mental revolution nahi. 'Mental' shabd se psychological testing wala option trap hai.

questions.question: Ek government office mein ek citizen ka form 3 hafte sirf isliye ruka rehta hai kyunki ek column galat font mein bhara gaya tha, jabki saari jaankari sahi thi. Ye kya dikhata hai?
options: Weber ki ideal bureaucracy jaisa hona chahiye waisa
Red tape: rules ka purpose bhool kar unka ritual
Fayol ka equity principle, sab par barabar rule
Taylor ka one best way, ek standard tareeka
questions.explanation: Weber ke liye rules fairness aur efficiency ke liye the. Jab rule ka purpose (sahi jaankari lena) poora ho chuka ho phir bhi chhoti formality par kaam ruke, to ye bureaucracy ka dysfunction, yaani red tape hai. Trap: 'ideal bureaucracy' wala option, kyunki rules follow ho rahe hain; par ideal type efficient hona chahiye, ritual nahi.

questions.question: Ek factory Taylor ka differential piece-rate use karti hai: daily standard 50 units; standard se kam par ₹4 per unit, aur standard ya usse zyada par ₹5 per unit (saare units par). Worker X ne 48 units banaaye aur worker Y ne 52. Y ne X se kitna zyada kamaaya?
questions.explanation: X standard se neeche hai: 48 × 4 = ₹192. Y standard se upar hai, isliye saare units par higher rate: 52 × 5 = ₹260. Fark = 260 − 192 = ₹68. ₹20 aur ₹16 dono ko same rate (₹5 ya ₹4) par 4 extra units maan kar aate hain, jo differential rate ka point hi miss karta hai. ₹52 sirf rate ka ₹1 fark Y ke 52 units par hai, X ke kam units ignore karke.

questions.question: 'Sitara Electronics' (fictional) mein do baatein hoti hain: (i) ek technician ko production head aur quality head dono se alag-alag orders milte hain; (ii) ek hi export order ke liye do departments apne-apne alag plan aur budget bana rahe hain. Fayol ke principles ke hisaab se kaunsa pair sahi hai?
options: (i) unity of command toota; (ii) unity of direction toota
(i) unity of direction toota; (ii) unity of command toota
(i) scalar chain toota; (ii) gang plank toota
Dono mein sirf unity of command toota hai
questions.explanation: (i) mein ek person ke do boss hain, jo unity of command ka violation hai. (ii) mein ek objective (export order) ke do plan aur do heads hain, jo unity of direction ka violation hai. Doosra option inhe ulta kar deta hai, jo sabse common trap hai. Gang plank toh same level ke logon ka seedha contact hai, iska yahan koi role nahi.

questions.question: Ek factory ne differential piece-rate lagaaya, par output nahi badha. Pata chala ki workers ke group ne aapas mein tay kar rakha tha ki koi bhi ek limit se zyada fast kaam nahi karega. Classical school ki kaunsi limitation ye case sabse achhe se dikhata hai?
options: Classical school mein planning ka koi role hi nahi tha
Worker ko sirf paise se chalne wala 'economic man' maanna
Classical school standardisation ke khilaaf tha
Classical thinkers ne written rules ko reject kiya
questions.explanation: Piece-rate is assumption par tika hai ki zyada paisa milega to worker zyada kaam karega ('economic man'). Yahan group ke social norms paise se zyada strong nikle, jo classical school ki social needs ignore karne wali limitation hai. Baaki options classical school ko ulta describe karte hain: usne planning, standardisation aur written rules par hi zor diya tha.

questions.question: Inme se kaunse teeno ideas Taylor ke scientific management ke hain (Fayol ya Weber ke nahi)?
options: Time study, scalar chain, esprit de corps
Unity of command, functional foremanship, impersonality
Time study, functional foremanship, differential piece-rate
Gang plank, rational-legal authority, motion study
questions.explanation: Time study, functional foremanship aur differential piece-rate teeno Taylor ke tools hain. Pehle option mein scalar chain aur esprit de corps Fayol ke principles hain. Doosre mein unity of command Fayol ka aur impersonality Weber ki hai. Chauthe mein gang plank Fayol ka, rational-legal authority Weber ki aur motion study Gilbreths ki hai. Har galat option mein ek-do sahi lagne wale naam mix kiye gaye hain.

weeks.title: Beyond the Classics: People, Numbers, Systems and Contingency
weeks.summary: Is week aap human relations movement (Hawthorne studies), behavioural school (Maslow, Herzberg, McGregor, Simon), quantitative approach, systems approach aur contingency approach seekhoge.
concepts: **Hawthorne studies**: Western Electric ke Hawthorne plant mein 1920s aur early 1930s mein experiments hue, jinse Elton Mayo aur unke colleagues jude the. Lighting experiments mein lighting badhao ya ghatao, output dono groups mein badh gaya. Conclusion: productivity sirf physical conditions se nahi, balki attention, group feeling aur social factors se bhi tay hoti hai. Observe kiye jaane se behaviour badalna **Hawthorne effect** kehlaata hai.

**Human relations insights**: Workers 'social man' hain, sirf 'economic man' nahi. **Informal groups** apne norms banate hain; bank wiring room observation mein group ne khud output ki ek limit tay kar rakhi thi aur usse zyada karne waale ko taane milte the. Communication, participation aur supervisor ka behaviour matter karta hai. Mary Parker Follett ne conflict ko dominate ya compromise karne ke bajaye **integration** se solve karne ki baat ki.

**Behavioural school (motivation)**: Abraham Maslow ki **need hierarchy**: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation; neeche ki need satisfy hone par upar wali motivate karti hai. Frederick Herzberg ka **two-factor theory**: **hygiene factors** (salary, policy, working conditions) ki kami dissatisfaction laati hai, par unke achhe hone se motivation nahi aata; **motivators** (achievement, recognition, kaam khud, responsibility, growth) asli motivation dete hain.

**McGregor ki Theory X aur Theory Y**: Douglas McGregor ne managers ki do assumptions bataayi. Theory X: log kaam se bachte hain, unhe control aur dhamki chahiye. Theory Y: log kaam ko natural maante hain, self-direction aur responsibility lete hain agar goals se committed hon. Manager ki assumption uske style ko shape karti hai.

**Simon aur Barnard**: Herbert Simon ne decision making ko administration ka centre maana. **Bounded rationality**: information, time aur dimaag ki limits ki wajah se manager perfect optimum nahi dhoondh paata, isliye woh **satisfice** karta hai, yaani pehla 'good enough' option chun leta hai. Chester Barnard ki **acceptance theory of authority**: authority tabhi kaam karti hai jab subordinate order ko accept kare.

**Quantitative approach (management science)**: Second World War mein operations research se aaya. Linear programming, queuing models, inventory models, simulation aur forecasting se decisions improve hote hain. Well-structured, measurable problems ke liye powerful, par human aur political factors ko pakadna mushkil.

**Systems approach**: Organisation ek **open system** hai jo environment se inputs (log, paisa, material, information) leta hai, unhe transform karta hai aur outputs deta hai, aur feedback se seekhta hai. Subsystems (departments) interdependent hain. Key ideas: **synergy** (whole parts ke sum se zyada), **entropy** (bina energy/input ke system bikharne lagta hai) aur **equifinality** (alag-alag raaston se same result tak pahuncha ja sakta hai).

**Contingency approach**: 'It depends.' Koi ek best way har jagah kaam nahi karta; sahi structure ya style situation par depend karta hai: environment, technology, size, log. Burns aur Stalker ne paaya ki stable environment mein **mechanistic** (rigid, rules-based) aur fast-changing environment mein **organic** (flexible, team-based) structure zyada kaam karta hai.

example.problem: 'Bharat Call Connect' (fictional) BPO mein manager ne har call ki strict monitoring aur late aane par fine shuru kiya. Teen mahine mein attrition badh gaya aur productivity gir gayi. Alag-alag schools isse kaise dekhenge?
steps: Classical/Theory X lens: manager ne maana ki log bina control ke kaam nahi karenge, isliye monitoring aur fines.
Human relations lens: strict surveillance ne team feeling aur informal group ka trust toda; social needs ignore hui.
Herzberg lens: fines aur monitoring hygiene side ko kharab karte hain, dissatisfaction badhta hai; recognition aur growth jaise motivators diye hi nahi gaye.
Systems lens: attrition badhne se hiring aur training ka load badha, naye log slow hain, isliye productivity aur giri; ek part ka change poore system ko hilaata hai.
Contingency lens: shayad ek rule-heavy approach routine back-office kaam mein chal jaaye, par complex customer calls mein flexibility chahiye.
Answer: Sirf control badhaane ke bajaye **motivators, team participation aur situation ke hisaab se design** chahiye; ye ek hi case mein kai schools ka combined use hai.

mistakes: Herzberg ke hygiene factors ko motivators samajhna. Salary badhaane se dissatisfaction kam ho sakta hai, par recognition, achievement aur growth ke bina motivation nahi aata.
Hawthorne ka conclusion 'lighting matter nahi karti' samajhna. Asli conclusion hai ki social aur psychological factors bhi output ko affect karte hain, sirf physical conditions nahi.
Equifinality aur synergy confuse karna. Synergy = whole > sum of parts. Equifinality = alag raaste, same result.
revision: Hawthorne: social factors aur attention se output badalta hai; informal group norms.
Maslow: 5-level hierarchy. Herzberg: hygiene vs motivators.
Theory X: control chahiye; Theory Y: self-direction.
Simon: bounded rationality, satisficing.
Open system: input, transformation, output, feedback; synergy, entropy, equifinality.
Contingency: it depends; mechanistic vs organic.

questions.question: Hawthorne studies ka sabse important conclusion kya tha?
options: Social factors aur attention productivity ko physical conditions jitna ya usse zyada affect karte hain
Lighting ki brightness productivity ka main factor hai
Paisa hi workers ka akela motivator hai
Strict rules se hamesha output badhta hai
questions.explanation: Lighting badhaane aur ghataane dono par output badha, jisse researchers ne samjha ki attention, group feeling aur social relations output ko affect karte hain. Lighting wala option trap hai: experiment shuru lighting se hua tha, par conclusion ulta nikla.

questions.question: Ek manager maanta hai ki uske employees kaam se bachte hain, responsibility nahi lena chahte, aur unhe close supervision aur punishment ka darr chahiye. McGregor ke hisaab se ye kaunsi assumption hai?
questions.explanation: Theory X ke assumptions hain ki log kaam pasand nahi karte aur unhe control, direction aur threat chahiye. Theory Y ulta maanti hai ki log self-directed aur responsible ho sakte hain. Hygiene factor Herzberg ka term hai aur satisficing Simon ka.

questions.question: 'Kaveri Software' (fictional) ne sabki salary badhaayi aur office canteen behtar kiya. Complaints kam ho gayi, par employees pehle se zyada motivated nahi hue. Herzberg ki theory isse kaise samjhaati hai?
options: Salary aur canteen motivators hain, isliye motivation badhna chahiye tha
Salary aur canteen hygiene factors hain: inse dissatisfaction hat-ta hai, par motivation nahi aata
Ye Theory X ki failure hai
questions.explanation: Herzberg ke hisaab se salary, working conditions aur policies hygiene factors hain; inki kami dissatisfaction deti hai, par inhe behtar karne se sirf 'no dissatisfaction' milta hai. Motivation ke liye achievement, recognition, responsibility aur growth chahiye. Pehla option sabse common trap hai, kyunki log paise ko motivator maan lete hain.

questions.question: Ek purchase manager ke paas 40 possible vendors hain. Woh sirf 3 ki quotes dekhta hai aur pehla vendor chun leta hai jo minimum quality aur price criteria poora karta hai. Herbert Simon ise kya kahenge?
options: Optimising, kyunki best vendor chuna gaya
questions.explanation: Time aur information limited hone ki wajah se manager sab 40 options compare nahi karta aur pehla 'good enough' option chunta hai. Simon ise satisficing kehte hain, jo bounded rationality ka result hai. Optimising tab hota jab sab options dekh kar best chuna jaata; yahan aisa nahi hua.

questions.question: Ek consultant kehta hai: 'Aapki electricity distribution company ke stable, rule-heavy kaam ke liye clear hierarchy aur rules theek hain, par aapki nayi app-based startup unit ko chhoti flexible teams chahiye.' Ye kis approach ki soch hai?
questions.explanation: Contingency approach kehta hai ki sahi structure situation par depend karta hai; stable environment mein mechanistic aur dynamic environment mein organic structure. Consultant ek hi company ke do units ko alag design de raha hai. Trap: bureaucracy, kyunki ek hissa rules ki baat karta hai, par bureaucracy har jagah ek hi model maanti hai.

questions.question: 'Sahyog Bank' (fictional) ki do branches ne same customer satisfaction score achieve kiya: ek ne extra staff rakh kar, doosri ne digital self-service kiosks laga kar. Open systems theory ka kaunsa concept ye dikhata hai?
questions.explanation: Equifinality ka matlab hai ki open system alag-alag starting points aur raaston se same final result tak pahunch sakta hai. Synergy sabse tempting trap hai, par woh 'whole parts ke sum se bada' wala idea hai, raaston ki variety ka nahi. Entropy system ke bikharne ki tendency hai.

questions.question: Maslow ki need hierarchy mein social needs ke theek upar kaunsi need aati hai?
questions.explanation: Order hai: physiological, safety, social, esteem, self-actualisation. Social ke theek upar esteem (respect, recognition) hai. Self-actualisation sabse upar hai, social ke theek upar nahi; safety aur physiological social se neeche hain.

questions.question: Ek naye billing software ki trial mein cashiers ko pata hai ki unhe observe kiya ja raha hai, aur woh normal se zyada dhyaan aur speed se kaam karte hain. Ise kya kehte hain?
questions.explanation: Observe kiye jaane ki wajah se behaviour badal jaana Hawthorne effect hai. Satisficing Simon ka 'good enough' option chunna hai aur bounded rationality uski wajah (limited information aur time); equifinality alag raaston se same result hai. Iska matlab ye bhi hai ki trial ke results normal din ke performance se zyada achhe dikh sakte hain.

questions.question: Open systems view mein ek hospital ke liye doctors, dawaiyan aur funds kya hain?
questions.explanation: Open system environment se log, material, paisa aur information inputs ke roop mein leta hai. Hospital in inputs ko treatment ke transformation process se outputs (theek hue patients) mein badalta hai. Trap: transformation process, kyunki doctors ilaaj karte hain; par doctors khud input hain, ilaaj ka kaam transformation hai.

questions.question: Ek manager ek naya order deta hai jo poori team ko unfair lagta hai. Team chupchaap use follow nahi karti, aur manager ki position hone ke bawajood order kaam nahi karta. Ye kis idea se sabse achhe se samajh aata hai?
options: Weber ki rational-legal authority ka idea
Fayol ka unity of command principle
Taylor ki mental revolution wali soch
questions.explanation: Barnard ke hisaab se authority upar se 'di' nahi jaati; woh tabhi kaam karti hai jab subordinates order ko accept karein. Yahan position hai par acceptance nahi, isliye authority fail hui. Trap: rational-legal authority, jo position aur rules se authority maanti hai; is case mein wahi position kaafi nahi nikli.

questions.question: Ek pharma company ki R&D unit mein har mahine nayi research findings aati hain aur projects baar-baar badalte hain. Burns aur Stalker is unit ke liye kaunsa structure suggest karte?
options: Mechanistic, kyunki research mein strict rules zaroori hain
Organic, kyunki environment tezi se badal raha hai
Tall structure, kyunki zyada levels se control badhta hai
questions.explanation: Burns aur Stalker ne paaya ki fast-changing environment mein organic (flexible, team-based) structure kaam karta hai, aur stable environment mein mechanistic. R&D unit ka environment har mahine badal raha hai. Trap: mechanistic ya bureaucratic, kyunki pharma regulated industry hai; par sawaal research unit ke changing kaam ke baare mein hai.

questions.question: Ek company 4 changes karti hai: (1) office ka AC theek karna, (2) best project ke liye sabke saamne recognition, (3) team leader banne aur zyada responsibility lene ka mauka, (4) leave policy saaf aur fair banana. Herzberg ke hisaab se inme se kaunse motivators hain?
questions.explanation: Recognition (2) aur responsibility/growth (3) motivators hain, jo asli motivation dete hain. AC yaani working conditions (1) aur company policy (4) hygiene factors hain: inse dissatisfaction kam hota hai, motivation nahi aata. Trap: 'saare chaaron', kyunki chaaron changes achhe hain; par Herzberg ke liye achha hona aur motivate karna alag baatein hain.

questions.question: Ravi ki job secure hai aur salary achhi hai, par naye shehar mein woh team mein bilkul akela feel karta hai. Maslow ke hisaab se abhi uski kaunsi need sabse zyada motivate karegi, aur manager ke liye sabse useful step kya hai?
options: Safety need; job security aur badhaana
Social need; use team activities aur group projects mein jodna
Self-actualisation; use turant sabse bada challenge dena
questions.explanation: Step 1: physiological (salary) aur safety (secure job) needs pehle se satisfied hain, aur Maslow ke hisaab se satisfied need motivate nahi karti. Step 2: agli unmet need social (belonging) hai, jo uske akelepan se dikh rahi hai. Isliye team mein jodna sabse useful hai. Salary ya security badhaana already satisfied needs par kharch hai, aur self-actualisation abhi do levels upar hai.

questions.question: Ek company ne linear programming se ek 'optimal' shift schedule banaaya jo labour cost 12% kam karta hai. Par usme family time ka koi dhyaan nahi tha; workers naraaz hue aur absenteeism itna badha ki saving khatam ho gayi. Sabse sahi analysis kya hai?
options: LP model galat tha, kyunki LP se kabhi bhi cost kam nahi hoti
Ye Hawthorne effect hai, kyunki workers ko observe kiya gaya
Ye satisficing hai, kyunki manager ne pehla good-enough schedule chuna
Model structured part mein sahi tha, par human factors miss kar gaya
questions.explanation: Quantitative approach measurable, structured problems (cost, hours) mein strong hai, par human aur social factors ko pakadna mushkil hai. Yahan maths sahi tha, par workers ki social needs (human relations lens) ignore hui, isliye real result bigad gaya. LP cost kam karne ka standard tool hai, isliye pehla option galat hai. Koi observation ya 'pehla good-enough option' kahani mein nahi hai, isliye Hawthorne aur satisficing traps hain.

questions.question: Ek NGO ne 3 saal se na naye volunteers liye, na training ki, na nayi funding li; dheere-dheere programmes band hone lage aur team bikharne lagi. Pehle jab uske teen chhote units ek saath kaam karte the, to unka total impact teeno ke alag-alag impact ke sum se zyada hota tha. Ye do observations kramashah kaunse concepts hain?
questions.explanation: Bina naye inputs (log, training, paisa) ke system ka dheere-dheere bikharna entropy hai. Units ka milkar apne alag-alag sum se zyada result dena synergy hai. Pehla option dono ko ulta karta hai. Equifinality alag raaston se same result tak pahunchna hai, jo kisi bhi observation mein nahi hai.

weeks.title: What Managers Do: The Functions of Management
weeks.summary: Is week aap management ke functions (planning, organising, staffing, leading, controlling) aur decision making seekhoge, saath mein span of control, delegation, control ke types aur Mintzberg ke managerial roles.
concepts: **Functions of management**: Fayol ne paanch functions diye the; baad mein Koontz aur O'Donnell jaise authors ne planning, organising, staffing, directing/leading aur controlling ka set popular kiya. Ye functions ek cycle hain aur har level ke manager (top, middle, first-line) karte hain, bas time ka mix alag hota hai.

**Planning**: Objectives tay karna aur unhe paane ka raasta decide karna. Levels: **strategic** (top, long-term), **tactical** (middle, departmental), **operational** (first-line, roz ka). Achhe objectives **SMART** hote hain (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound). **Standing plans** baar-baar use hote hain (policy, procedure, rule); **single-use plans** ek baar ke liye (programme, project, budget). Drucker ka **management by objectives (MBO)**: manager aur subordinate milkar goals tay karte hain aur unhi par performance judge hoti hai.

**Organising**: Kaam ko activities mein todna, unhe departments mein group karna, authority-responsibility assign karna aur coordination banana. **Span of control** = ek manager ke under kitne log. Narrow span se **tall** structure (zyada levels), wide span se **flat** structure (kam levels). **Centralisation** mein decisions upar, **decentralisation** mein neeche.

**Delegation**: Manager kaam ke saath **authority** neeche de sakta hai, par apni **accountability** poori tarah nahi de sakta; subordinate manager ke prati jawabdeh hai aur manager apne boss ke prati. Line authority direct command chain hai; staff (jaise legal, HR advisors) advice dete hain.

**Staffing aur leading**: Staffing = manpower planning, recruitment, selection, training, appraisal aur compensation. Leading/directing = motivation, leadership, communication aur supervision. Leadership styles: **autocratic** (manager akela decide), **democratic** (team ki participation), **laissez-faire** (team ko poori freedom).

**Controlling**: Chaar steps: standards set karo, actual performance measure karo, standard se compare karo, aur deviation par corrective action lo. Timing ke hisaab se: **feedforward** (kaam shuru hone se pehle, jaise raw material check), **concurrent** (kaam ke dauraan) aur **feedback** (kaam ke baad). **Management by exception**: sirf significant deviations upar report hon.

**Decision making**: Steps: problem pehchaano, alternatives banao, evaluate karo, best chuno, implement karo, result review karo. **Programmed decisions** routine aur repetitive hote hain (reorder level par stock mangwana); **non-programmed decisions** naye aur unstructured (naye country mein entry). Upar ke levels par non-programmed zyada.

**Roles aur skills**: Henry Mintzberg ne managers ko observe karke 10 roles teen groups mein diye: interpersonal (figurehead, leader, liaison), informational (monitor, disseminator, spokesperson) aur decisional (entrepreneur, disturbance handler, resource allocator, negotiator). Robert Katz ki skills: technical, human aur conceptual; upar jaate-jaate conceptual skill ki zaroorat badhti hai.

example.problem: 'Swaad Tiffin Services' (fictional) Bengaluru mein 2 naye kitchens khol rahi hai. Har action ko sahi management function mein daalo: (a) agle 6 mahine mein 3,000 daily orders ka target aur budget banana, (b) har kitchen mein head chef, packing aur delivery teams banana aur reporting line tay karna, (c) 25 cooks hire karke hygiene training dena, (d) team meeting mein staff ko motivate karna aur naye menu ka plan samjhana, (e) har hafte actual orders aur customer complaints ko target se compare karna.
steps: (a) Target aur budget tay karna future ka raasta decide karna hai, yaani **planning**.
(b) Teams banana aur reporting lines tay karna **organising** hai.
(c) Hiring aur training **staffing** hai.
(d) Motivate karna aur communicate karna **leading/directing** hai.
(e) Actual ko target se compare karna **controlling** hai; agar orders kam hain to corrective action (jaise marketing push) lena bhi controlling ka hissa hai.
Answer: a = planning, b = organising, c = staffing, d = leading, e = **controlling**.

mistakes: Planning aur controlling ko alag-alag dibbe samajhna. Controlling ke standards planning se aate hain, aur controlling ka feedback agle planning cycle mein jaata hai; dono ek loop hain.
Ye maanna ki delegate karne ke baad manager ki zimmedari khatam. Authority delegate hoti hai, accountability nahi.
Wide span of control ko hamesha achha samajhna. Wide span flat aur fast hai, par agar kaam complex hai ya subordinates naye hain to manager overload ho jaata hai.
revision: Functions: planning, organising, staffing, leading, controlling.
Standing plans: policy, procedure, rule. Single-use: programme, project, budget.
Narrow span = tall structure; wide span = flat structure.
Authority delegate hoti hai, accountability nahi.
Control: feedforward (pehle), concurrent (dauraan), feedback (baad).
Mintzberg: interpersonal, informational, decisional roles.

questions.question: Ek branch manager monthly sales ko target se compare karta hai, 15% shortfall dekhta hai aur kaaran dhoondh kar corrective steps leta hai. Ye kaunsa function hai?
questions.explanation: Actual performance ko standard se compare karna aur deviation par corrective action lena controlling ke steps hain. Trap: planning, kyunki target planning se aaya tha, par yahan target banaya nahi ja raha, check kiya ja raha hai.

questions.question: Factory ka niyam 'Production floor par mobile phone allowed nahi' kis type ka plan hai?
questions.explanation: Rule ek standing plan hai jo baar-baar har situation mein lagta hai aur batata hai kya karna hai ya kya nahi; isme discretion nahi hoti. Budget, programme aur project single-use plans hain jo ek specific purpose ke baad khatam ho jaate hain.

questions.question: Do companies mein 1,000 employees hain. Company A mein har manager 4 logon ko supervise karta hai, Company B mein 20 logon ko. Kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Company A flatter hogi kyunki uske managers par kam load hai
Company B ko zyada hierarchical levels chahiye honge
Company A mein zyada levels honge (tall structure) aur B flatter hogi
Span of control ka levels ki sankhya par koi asar nahi
questions.explanation: Narrow span (4) mein har level par kam log aate hain, isliye 1,000 logon tak pahunchne ke liye zyada levels chahiye: CEO samet lagbhag 6 levels, jabki span 20 mein 4 levels kaafi hain. Isliye A tall aur B flat. Trap: 'kam load = flat' sochna; asal mein narrow span se structure taller banta hai.

questions.question: Ek manager ne client report banane ka kaam apne assistant ko delegate kiya. Report mein galti thi aur woh client tak pahunch gayi. Manager ke boss ke saamne ultimately kaun accountable hai?
options: Manager, kyunki accountability poori tarah delegate nahi hoti
Sirf assistant, kyunki kaam usne kiya
Client, kyunki usne report accept ki
questions.explanation: Delegation mein authority neeche jaati hai, par manager apne boss ke prati accountable rehta hai. Assistant manager ke prati jawabdeh hai, par boss ke saamne zimmedari manager ki hai. Trap: 'jisne kaam kiya wahi poora zimmedar', jo delegation ka sabse common misunderstanding hai.

questions.question: Ek restaurant har subah sabzi aur dairy ki delivery aate hi quality check karta hai, aur kharab maal cooking se pehle hi wapas kar deta hai. Ye kis type ka control hai?
questions.explanation: Problem ko process shuru hone se pehle, inputs ke level par rokna feedforward control hai. Concurrent control cooking ke dauraan hota (jaise chef ka taste check), aur feedback control khaana serve hone ke baad (jaise customer reviews). Trap: concurrent, kyunki check subah roz hota hai, par timing cooking se pehle ki hai.

questions.question: Ek plant manager ka poora din contract workers ki achanak hadtaal suljhaane aur boiler kharab hone ke baad shifts dobara arrange karne mein jaata hai. Mintzberg ke hisaab se woh mainly kaunsa role nibha raha hai?
questions.explanation: Achanak aayi crisis (strike, machine breakdown) ko handle karna disturbance handler role hai, jo decisional group mein aata hai. Spokesperson trap hai: woh role bahar ke logon (media, investors) ko organisation ki taraf se information dena hai, crisis suljhaana nahi. Figurehead ceremonial kaam hai, jaise ribbon cutting.

questions.question: Ek supermarket ka floor supervisor kal ke liye staff ki shifts aur shelf restocking ka schedule banata hai. Ye kis level ki planning hai?
questions.explanation: First-line manager ka roz ka, short-term schedule operational planning hai. Strategic planning top level par long-term direction hai, aur tactical planning middle level par departmental plans. Trap: tactical, kyunki schedule ek plan hai; par time-frame sirf ek din ka aur level first-line ka hai.

questions.question: Ek team leader har important decision se pehle team ki raay leta hai aur discussion ke baad team ke saath milkar decide karta hai. Ye kaunsa leadership style hai?
questions.explanation: Team ki participation ke saath decision lena democratic style hai. Autocratic mein manager akela decide karta hai, aur laissez-faire mein team ko poori freedom milti hai aur leader khud zyada involve nahi hota. Theory X ek assumption hai, leadership style nahi.

questions.question: Ek dukaan ka system aisa hai ki stock 200 units se neeche jaate hi apne aap 1,000 units ka order chala jaata hai. Ye kis type ka decision hai?
questions.explanation: Routine, repetitive decision jiske liye pehle se rule bana hai, programmed decision hai; reorder level par stock mangwana iska classic example hai. Non-programmed decisions naye aur unstructured hote hain, jaise naye country mein entry. Strategic aur creative options bhi naye, one-time sochne waale decisions ki taraf ishaara karte hain.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa objective SMART hai?
options: Hum har department mein customer service ko behtar banaayenge
Hum agle kuch time mein jitna ho sake sales badhaayenge
31 March tak average delivery time 4 din se 2 din karna
Hum jald hi apni industry ke market leader ban jaayenge
questions.explanation: SMART = specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound. Delivery time 4 se 2 din ka goal specific aur measurable hai, aur 31 March ki deadline time-bound banaati hai. Baaki teeno vague hain: 'behtar', 'jitna ho sake' aur 'jald hi' na naape ja sakte hain na unki clear deadline hai.

questions.question: Ek nayi factory supervisor machine settings bahut achhe se jaanti hai, jabki CEO ko poori industry aur company ke alag parts ke aapas ke rishte samajhne padte hain. Katz ke hisaab se manager jitna upar jaata hai, kaunsi skill ki zaroorat utni hi badhti hai?
questions.explanation: Katz ke hisaab se upar ke levels par conceptual skill (poori organisation aur environment ko ek saath samajhna) sabse zyada chahiye. Technical skill neeche ke levels par sabse zyada kaam aati hai, jaise supervisor ki machine knowledge. Human skill har level par chahiye, isliye woh 'upar jaate-jaate badhne' wali skill nahi. Operational skill Katz ki teen skills mein hai hi nahi.

questions.question: Ek company mein har manager ke under exactly 5 log hain. CEO samet 4 management levels hain aur sabse neeche workers ka ek level hai (workers ke under koi nahi). Workers kitne hain? Agar span 10 kar diya jaaye, to itne hi workers ke liye CEO samet kam se kam kitne management levels chahiye honge?
questions.explanation: Span 5: CEO 1 → 5 → 25 → 125 managers (4 levels), aur 125 × 5 = 625 workers. Span 10: 625 ÷ 10 = 62.5, yaani 63 managers; 63 ÷ 10 = 6.3, yaani 7 managers; 7 ko 1 CEO sambhaal leta hai, isliye 3 levels. 2 levels sirf 10 × 10 = 100 workers sambhaal sakte hain, jo 625 se kam hai. 125 workers aakhri management level ko workers maan lene ki galti hai, aur 3,125 ek extra level gin lene se aata hai. Lesson: wide span se structure flat hota hai.

questions.question: Ek bakery ke teen checks: (P) baking ke dauraan har 10 minute oven ka temperature check karna, (Q) aata delivery par hi moisture aur quality ke liye check karna, (R) din ke end mein customer complaints gin kar review karna. P, Q aur R kramashah kis type ke control hain?
questions.explanation: P kaam ke dauraan ho raha hai, isliye concurrent. Q process shuru hone se pehle inputs ka check hai, isliye feedforward. R kaam poora hone ke baad ka result dekhta hai, isliye feedback. Trap: pehla option, jo 'pehle, dauraan, baad' ka order P, Q, R par seedha laga deta hai bina har check ki timing dekhe.

questions.question: Ek plant head ke din ke teen kaam: (1) union ke saath wage agreement par baat-cheet, (2) naye budget mein kis department ko kitna paisa mile ye tay karna, (3) local school ke annual function mein company ki taraf se chief guest banna. Mintzberg ke roles kramashah kaunse hain?
questions.explanation: (1) Union ke saath bargaining negotiator role hai (decisional). (2) Budget mein paisa baantna resource allocator hai (decisional). (3) Ceremonial kaam mein organisation ko represent karna figurehead hai (interpersonal). Trap: spokesperson, kyunki function mein woh company ki taraf se bolta hai; par spokesperson information dene ka role hai, ceremonial presence ka nahi. Disturbance handler achanak aayi crisis ke liye hai, planned wage talks ke liye nahi.

questions.question: Ek sales head quarter ki shuruaat mein har area manager ke saath baith kar unke targets milkar tay karta hai, aur quarter ke end mein appraisal sirf inhi targets par hota hai. Beech mein sirf woh area jo target se 30% ya zyada peeche ho, uski detailed report upar jaati hai. Yahan kaunse do ideas use ho rahe hain?
questions.explanation: Manager aur subordinate ka milkar goals tay karna aur unhi par performance judge karna Drucker ka MBO hai. Sirf significant deviation (30% ya zyada) ko upar report karna management by exception hai. Theory X aur autocratic style participation ke ulta hain. Feedforward control trap hai: targets pehle bante hain, par yahan reporting kaam ke dauraan aur baad ke deviation par hai, inputs ke check par nahi.

weeks.title: Business Functions and How They Fit Together
weeks.summary: Is week aap business ke main functional areas (operations, marketing, finance, HR, information systems) seekhoge, Porter ki value chain samjhoge, aur dekhoge ki ye functions aapas mein kaise judte aur takraate hain.
concepts: **Functional areas**: Har business kuch core kaam karta hai: cheez banana (operations), bechna (marketing), paisa manage karna (finance), logon ko manage karna (HR) aur information sambhalna (information systems). Ye organisation ke subsystems hain; management functions (planning, organising...) in sab ke andar chalte hain.

**Operations**: Inputs (material, labour, machines) ko outputs (goods/services) mein badalna. Decisions: capacity, process design, quality, inventory aur supply chain. Production types: job (ek-ek custom order), batch, mass aur continuous (refinery jaise). **Productivity** = output ÷ input, jaise units per labour-hour.

**Marketing**: Customer ki needs samajhna aur value deliver karna. **STP**: segmentation (market ko groups mein baantna), targeting (kaunsa group chuna), positioning (customer ke mann mein kya image). E. Jerome McCarthy ke **4Ps**: product, price, place (distribution), promotion. Services ke liye people, process aur physical evidence jod kar 7Ps.

**Finance**: Teen core decisions: **investment decision** (paisa kahan lagaayein, jaise nayi machine; capital budgeting), **financing decision** (paisa kahan se laayein: debt ya equity) aur **dividend decision** (profit shareholders ko dein ya business mein rakhein). Saath mein **working capital** management: liquidity aur profitability ka balance.

**Human resource management**: Sahi log laana, develop karna, motivate aur retain karna. Recruitment (candidates ka pool banana) aur selection (pool mein se chunna) alag steps hain. Training, performance appraisal, compensation aur employee relations bhi HR mein aate hain.

**Information systems**: **TPS** (transaction processing, jaise billing), **MIS** (managers ke liye regular reports), **DSS** (what-if analysis se decision support) aur **ERP** (saare functions ek common database par, jisse ek order ka data sales, inventory aur accounts mein ek saath update ho). Data se information banti hai, information se decisions.

**Value chain (Michael Porter)**: Primary activities: inbound logistics, operations, outbound logistics, marketing and sales, service. Support activities: firm infrastructure (finance, planning, legal), HRM, technology development aur procurement. Competitive advantage in activities ko behtar karne aur aapas mein jodne se aata hai.

**Interdependence aur conflict**: Marketing variety aur fast delivery chahta hai, operations long production runs aur standard products, finance kam inventory aur kam cost, HR stable staffing. Har function apna target alag se optimise kare to poori company ko nuksaan ho sakta hai, isliye cross-functional teams aur joint planning (jaise sales and operations planning) zaroori hain.

example.problem: 'Kaveri Garments' (fictional) ne March mein 2,400 labour-hours lagakar 12,000 shirts banaayi, aur April mein 2,500 labour-hours lagakar 13,500 shirts. Labour productivity kitni badhi?
steps: Labour productivity = output ÷ labour-hours.
March: 12,000 ÷ 2,400 = 5 shirts per labour-hour.
April: 13,500 ÷ 2,500 = 5.4 shirts per labour-hour.
Dhyaan do: output 12.5% badha, par hours bhi badhe, isliye productivity utni nahi badhi.
Answer: Labour productivity **8%** badhi.

mistakes: Output badhne ko productivity badhna samajhna. Productivity ratio hai; agar input bhi utna hi badha to productivity same reh sakti hai.
Investment aur financing decision mix karna. 'Kya khareedein / kahan lagaayein' = investment. 'Paisa kahan se laayein' = financing.
Har function ko alag island samajhna. Exam ke case questions mein aksar sahi answer wahi hota hai jo functions ke beech coordination ki baat kare.
revision: Functional areas: operations, marketing, finance, HR, information systems.
Productivity = output ÷ input.
4Ps: product, price, place, promotion; STP: segment, target, position.
Finance: investment, financing, dividend decisions + working capital.
ERP: saare functions ek common database par.
Value chain: 5 primary + 4 support activities.

questions.question: Ek company decide kar rahi hai ki nayi machine ke liye bank loan le ya naye shares issue kare. Ye finance ka kaunsa decision hai?
questions.explanation: Paisa kahan se laana hai (debt vs equity) ye financing decision hai. Machine khareedni hai ya nahi, woh investment decision hota; yahan woh pehle hi tay hai. Trap: 'machine' shabd dekh kar investment chun lena.

questions.question: 'Mithas Sweets' (fictional) apni dukaanon ke alawa ab quick-commerce apps ke through bhi mithai bechna shuru karti hai. Marketing mix ka kaunsa P badla?
questions.explanation: Product customer tak kis channel se pahunchta hai, ye place (distribution) hai. Product, price aur promotion yahan same hain; sirf naya sales channel juda hai. Trap: promotion, kyunki apps par dikhna advertising jaisa lagta hai, par yahan maal bikne ka channel badla hai.

questions.question: Ek unit ne week 1 mein 600 labour-hours mein 4,800 units banaaye aur week 2 mein 560 labour-hours mein 5,040 units. Labour productivity mein kitna change hua?
questions.explanation: Week 1: 4,800 ÷ 600 = 8 units per hour. Week 2: 5,040 ÷ 560 = 9 units per hour. Change = (9 − 8) ÷ 8 = 12.5% increase. 5% sirf output ka change hai (hours ignore kiye), 6.7% hours ki kami hai, aur 11.1% galat base (9) se divide karne par aata hai.

questions.question: Porter ki value chain mein poori company ke liye employees ki recruitment aur training kis activity mein aati hai?
questions.explanation: HRM ek support activity hai jo saari primary activities ko support karti hai; recruitment, training aur compensation isi mein aate hain. Trap: operations, kyunki trained log factory mein kaam karte hain, par value chain mein HR ka kaam alag support activity mana jaata hai.

questions.question: Marketing customers ko custom colours aur 3-day delivery ka promise karta hai. Operations shikaayat karta hai ki baar-baar machine changeover se cost badh rahi hai, aur finance ko badhti inventory ki chinta hai. Ye situation sabse achhe se kya dikhaati hai?
options: Functions interdependent hain; ek function ka apna target alag se optimise karna doosron ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai, isliye coordination chahiye
Marketing ka kaam sirf advertising hai, isliye use delivery ka promise nahi karna chahiye
Operations aur finance ka aapas mein koi sambandh nahi hai
Ye sirf HR ki problem hai, kyunki staff kam hai
questions.explanation: Ek function ka decision (marketing ka promise) doosre functions ke cost aur inventory par asar daal raha hai; ye functional interdependence hai. Iska solution joint planning hai, jaise sales and operations planning. Baaki options ya to marketing ko galat define karte hain ya functions ko alag islands maante hain.

questions.question: Ek company mein sales, inventory aur accounts ke alag-alag software hain. Ek hi order teen baar type hota hai aur teeno jagah ke numbers aksar match nahi karte. Kaunsa information system is root cause ko sabse achhe se solve karega?
options: Har department ke liye ek aur alag TPS
ERP: saare functions ke liye ek integrated common database
Data entry ke liye aur staff
Sirf top management ke liye DSS
questions.explanation: Root cause data ka alag-alag systems mein bikhra hona hai. ERP ek common database par sab functions ko jodta hai, isliye order ek baar enter hota hai aur sab jagah update. Aur TPS ya aur staff problem ko badhaayenge ya sirf chhupaayenge, aur DSS analysis ke liye hai, data integration ke liye nahi.

questions.question: Ek oil refinery 24 ghante, saal bhar bina ruke ek hi tarah ka output banati rehti hai. Ye kaunsa production type hai?
questions.explanation: Bina ruke, lagaataar flow mein ek hi product banana continuous production hai; refinery iska standard example hai. Job production ek-ek custom order hai aur batch production groups mein. Trap: mass production, jo bhi bade volume ka hai, par usme alag-alag discrete units (jaise cars) bante hain, lagaataar flow nahi.

questions.question: Ek company job portal par ad daal kar ek post ke liye 500 applications ikattha karti hai. HR ka ye step kya kehlaata hai?
questions.explanation: Candidates ka pool banana recruitment hai. Us pool mein se interviews aur tests ke baad sahi log chunna selection hai, jo agla step hai. Trap: selection, kyunki dono hiring ke steps hain; par 500 applications ikattha karna abhi kisi ko chunna nahi hai.

questions.question: Ek e-commerce company apne warehouse se finished orders pack karke customers tak bhejti hai. Porter ki value chain mein ye kaunsi activity hai?
questions.explanation: Finished product ko customer tak pahunchaana outbound logistics hai. Inbound logistics suppliers se aane wale material ko receive aur store karna hai. Procurement inputs khareedne ki support activity hai. Trap: inbound, kyunki dono mein warehouse hai; farak direction ka hai: andar aana vs bahar jaana.

questions.question: Ek company ne is saal ₹20 crore profit kamaaya. Board tay kar raha hai ki isme se kitna shareholders ko dein aur kitna business mein rok kar rakhein. Ye finance ka kaunsa decision hai?
questions.explanation: Profit ko shareholders mein baantna ya business mein retain karna dividend decision hai. Investment decision tab hota jab sawaal ho ki paisa kis asset ya project mein lagaayein. Trap: financing, kyunki retained profit bhi ek source of funds ban jaata hai; par yahan core sawaal profit ka bantwaara hai.

questions.question: Ek shampoo brand chahta hai ki customers ke mann mein uski image 'hard water ke liye bana shampoo' ki bane. STP mein ye kaunsa step hai?
questions.explanation: Customer ke mann mein brand ki ek specific image banana positioning hai. Segmentation market ko groups mein baantna hai, aur targeting un groups mein se ek chunna (jaise hard water wale shehar). Trap: promotion, jo 4Ps ka hissa hai; ads us positioning ko communicate karte hain, par STP ka step positioning hi hai.

questions.question: 'Nirmal Bottles' (fictional) ne January mein 2,000 machine-hours mein 60,000 bottles banaayi, aur February mein 2,400 machine-hours mein 66,000 bottles. Machine productivity (bottles per machine-hour) mein kya change hua?
questions.explanation: January: 60,000 ÷ 2,000 = 30 bottles per machine-hour. February: 66,000 ÷ 2,400 = 27.5. Change = (27.5 − 30) ÷ 30 = −2.5 ÷ 30 ≈ −8.3%. 10% sirf output ka increase hai aur 20% sirf input ka; dono ratio ignore karte hain. 9.1% galat base (27.5) se divide karne par aata hai. Lesson: output badha, phir bhi productivity giri.

questions.question: Teen systems: (1) supermarket ki billing jo har sale record karti hai, (2) har Monday regional managers ko jaane wali standard weekly sales report, (3) ek tool jisme manager dekhta hai ki 'agar price 5% ghataayein to profit par kya asar padega'. Ye kramashah kaunse information systems hain?
questions.explanation: (1) Roz ke transactions record karna TPS hai. (2) Managers ke liye regular, fixed format reports MIS hai. (3) What-if analysis se decision mein madad DSS hai. Trap: (2) ko DSS maanna, kyunki report decision mein kaam aati hai; par fixed weekly report MIS hai, DSS interactive what-if ke liye hai. ERP integrated database hai, aur in teeno mein se kisi ka description nahi.

questions.question: Ek production line hafte mein 50 hours available hai aur chalte waqt 100 units per hour banati hai. Har colour change par 2 hours setup lagta hai, jisme production band rehta hai. Abhi hafte mein 5 colours bante hain (5 changeovers). Marketing 10 colours chahta hai. Weekly output kitne % girega?
questions.explanation: Abhi: setup = 5 × 2 = 10 hours, production = 50 − 10 = 40 hours, output = 4,000 units. 10 colours: setup = 20 hours, production = 30 hours, output = 3,000 units. Girawat = 1,000 ÷ 4,000 = 25%. 20% extra setup hours (10) ko total 50 hours se divide karne ki galti hai, aur 50% colours double hone se seedha output aadha maan lena. Ye marketing aur operations ke conflict ko numbers mein dikhata hai, isliye joint planning chahiye.

questions.question: Ek furniture company ki chaar activities: (1) lakdi suppliers ke saath kharid ke contracts negotiate karna, (2) factory mein furniture banana, (3) naya design software develop karna, (4) customers ke ghar furniture install aur repair karna. Porter ki value chain mein inme se kaunsi support activities hain?
questions.explanation: (1) Inputs khareedna procurement hai aur (3) design software banana technology development hai: dono support activities. (2) Furniture banana operations hai aur (4) install aur repair service hai: dono primary activities. Trap: (4) ko support maanna, kyunki woh sale ke baad ka 'support' lagta hai; par value chain mein after-sales service ek primary activity hai.

weeks.title: The Art of Thinking: Framing, Mental Models and Biases
weeks.summary: Is week aap seekhoge ki problem ko kaise frame karein, hidden assumptions aur mental models kaise pehchaanein, ladder of inference kya hai, aur managerial decisions mein common cognitive biases (anchoring, confirmation, sunk cost, framing, groupthink) se kaise bachein.
concepts: **Problem framing**: Problem ko jaise define karoge, waise hi solutions dikhenge. 'Hume aur salesmen chahiye' ek solution ko problem bana deta hai; 'Sales kyun gir rahi hai?' poori problem kholta hai. **Symptom** (late deliveries) aur **underlying problem** (galat route planning) alag hote hain. Reframe karne ka simple tareeka: 'Hum kaise ... kar sakte hain?' ya 'Ye problem kiske liye hai aur kyun?'

**Assumptions**: Har plan ke peeche kuch maani hui baatein hoti hain, jaise 'customers sirf sasta chahte hain' ya 'competitor price nahi ghataayega'. Achha manager unhe likh kar check karta hai: kaunsi assumption galat hui to plan fail hoga?

**Mental models**: Dimaag mein bani duniya ki simplified picture, jo batati hai ki cheezein kaise kaam karti hain. Ye fast decisions mein madad karte hain, par purane ho jaayein to galat raasta dikhate hain. Peter Senge ne mental models ko surface aur test karna learning organisation ki ek discipline maana.

**Ladder of inference**: Chris Argyris ka model: hum observable data mein se kuch data chunte hain, uska meaning nikaalte hain, assumptions jodte hain, conclusion banate hain, beliefs banate hain aur phir action lete hain. Beliefs agli baar kaunsa data chunenge use bhi affect karte hain (reflexive loop). Bachaav: seedhi par neeche utro aur poocho 'iska data kya hai?'

**System 1 aur System 2**: Daniel Kahneman ke hisaab se System 1 fast, automatic aur intuitive hai; System 2 slow, effortful aur logical. Biases zyada tar System 1 ke shortcuts (heuristics) se aate hain; important decisions mein System 2 ko jaan-boojh kar lagana padta hai.

**Common cognitive biases**: **Anchoring** (pehla number judgement ko kheench leta hai), **confirmation bias** (sirf woh info dhoondhna jo apni raay support kare), **availability** (jo yaad mein aasaani se aaye use zyada likely maanna), **sunk cost fallacy** (jo kharch ho chuka uski wajah se galat project chalate rehna), **framing effect** (same fact alag shabdon mein alag decision dilaata hai), **overconfidence** aur **status quo bias**.

**Groupthink**: Irving Janis ka concept: bahut cohesive group mein log harmony bachaane ke liye doubts nahi bolte, aur group galat decision par 'sab agreed' dikhta hai. Signs: illusion of unanimity, dissent ko daba dena. Remedies: devil's advocate, leader apni raay last mein de, outside experts.

**Debiasing tools**: Sunk cost se bachne ke liye sirf future costs aur benefits compare karo. Anchoring se bachne ke liye pehle apna independent estimate banao. **Pre-mortem** (Gary Klein): maan lo project fail ho gaya, ab socho kyun hua. 'Consider the opposite', checklists aur base rates bhi kaam aate hain.

example.problem: 'Zippy Scooters' (fictional) ek EV model par ₹40 crore kharch kar chuki hai. Launch tak ₹25 crore aur lagenge. Competitor ke behtar model ke baad estimate hai ki launch se aage sirf ₹20 crore ka total benefit aayega (present value mein). CEO kehta hai 'itna lag chuka hai, ab rukna bewakoofi hai.' Sahi decision kya hai?
steps: ₹40 crore sunk cost hai: project chale ya ruke, woh wapas nahi aayega. Isliye decision mein uska koi role nahi.
Continue karne ka future cost = ₹25 crore; future benefit = ₹20 crore.
Net effect of continuing = 20 − 25 = −₹5 crore.
Rukne par net future effect = 0 (aur team ko kisi behtar project mein lagaaya ja sakta hai).
CEO ki line sunk cost fallacy hai: past kharch ko future decision ka reason banana.
Answer: Project **rok do**; kyunki aage badhne par ₹5 crore ka extra loss hai.

mistakes: Sunk cost ko 'investment bachaana' samajhna. Jo paisa wapas nahi aa sakta, use future decision mein mat jodo; sirf aage ke costs aur benefits dekho.
Anchoring aur framing ko same samajhna. Anchoring mein ek starting **number** judgement kheenchta hai; framing mein same fact ko **shabdon** ke alag tareeke se rakhne par decision badalta hai.
Symptom ko problem maan kar solve karna. Pehle 'kyun' poocho, phir solution socho.
revision: Framing: problem ki definition solutions tay karti hai.
Ladder of inference: data → selected data → meaning → assumptions → conclusions → beliefs → actions.
System 1 fast/intuitive, System 2 slow/logical.
Anchoring = pehla number; confirmation = apni raay ka saboot dhoondhna.
Sunk cost: past kharch ignore karo, future compare karo.
Groupthink se bachao: devil's advocate, leader last mein bole.

questions.question: Ek office space ka seller shuru mein ₹50 lakh maangta hai, jabki similar spaces ₹30 lakh ke aas-paas bikte hain. Buyer negotiate karke ₹45 lakh par khush hai ki 'achha deal mila'. Kaunsa bias kaam kar raha hai?
questions.explanation: Pehla number (₹50 lakh) anchor ban gaya aur buyer ne deal ko us anchor se compare kiya, market value se nahi. Confirmation bias apni maujooda raay ke saboot dhoondhne ka hai, aur availability yaad mein aasaani se aane waali cheezon ka; yahan dono ka role nahi.

questions.question: Ek purchase head apne pasandeeda vendor ke favour wali reports dhyaan se padhta hai, par us vendor ki late deliveries wali complaints ko 'ek-do baar ki baat' keh kar chhod deta hai. Ye kaunsa bias hai?
questions.explanation: Apni pehle se bani raay ko support karne wali information ko weight dena aur ulti information ko dismiss karna confirmation bias hai. Groupthink ek group ka phenomenon hai, jabki yahan ek individual ka judgement hai. Sunk cost tab hota jab past kharch ki wajah se vendor ke saath bana rehta.

questions.question: Ek company ek software project par ₹8 crore kharch kar chuki hai. Use poora karne ke liye ₹3 crore aur chahiye, aur poora hone par ₹2 crore ka benefit milega. Ek ready-made software ₹1 crore mein wahi ₹2 crore ka benefit deta hai. Rational decision kya hai?
options: Project chhodo aur ready-made software lo
Project poora karo, kyunki ₹8 crore pehle hi lag chuke hain
Project poora karo, kyunki total ₹11 crore ka system milega
Kuch mat karo: na project, na ready-made software
questions.explanation: ₹8 crore sunk hai, isliye sirf future dekho. Project poora karne par 2 − 3 = −₹1 crore; ready-made par 2 − 1 = +₹1 crore; kuch na karne par 0. Sabse achha ready-made hai. 'Pehle hi lag chuke hain' wala option seedha sunk cost fallacy hai, aur '₹11 crore ka system' cost ko value samajhne ki galti hai.

questions.question: Board ke saamne ek restructuring plan do tareeke se rakha gaya: 'Is plan se 90% jobs bachengi' aur 'Is plan se 10% jobs jaayengi'. Board pehle version ko approve karta hai aur doosre ko reject. Ye kaunsa effect hai?
questions.explanation: Dono statements ka matlab bilkul same hai; sirf gain (bachengi) aur loss (jaayengi) ki language alag hai. Same fact ki presentation se decision badalna framing effect hai. Anchoring trap hai kyunki numbers dikh rahe hain, par yahan koi starting number judgement ko kheench nahi raha.

questions.question: Ek supervisor ne dekha ki ek naya employee do din late aaya. Usne socha 'ise job ki parwaah nahi', aur use important projects dena band kar diya.
